questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses avaliable at the university and the weather

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, QUT helps alot and was easy to communicate with via. e-mail when I had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up at the airport and driven to my accomodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The course catalogue for selecting courses where a bit difficult to navigate, but only because there were so many courses avaliable.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I booked my accomodation with Student One Wharf Street a few months in advance. It was easy, because I was early, some of my friends had a very hard time finding accomodation because of the housing crisis in Brisbane.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed living at Student One, even though it was less social than I had hoped and very expensive, but it was right in the business/city center which was incredible to experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because of the prices and that you have to be early/lucky.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to select courses and register at a certain time. I don't remember it being too difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could e-mail student help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted and was able to swap during the semester, when I realised I had chosen a course that was not for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time researching the courses and think about whats interesting, but also don't take on too large of a study load.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My courses were really interesting and i learned a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were different than my experiences in Denmark, mainly because of many assesments during the semester and a smaller load during the exam period, which turned out to be great and gave me time to travel during the semester and exam period.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, but very few students showed up to class because everything was recorded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian Health System
Health Systems 
Contemporary Health Management
Quality Management in Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially Contemporaty Health Management and Quality Management in Health were very interesting and nothing i had come close to during my education at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wanted to travel a lot, which cost me more than I had anticipated, but it was worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food (but also because I ate out a lot)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went with the skiing club on a weekend beach trip, which was very fun. Also check out QUEST, which is the student club for University of Queensland, but they do pubnights every week, that were a good way to meet other international students from both universities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Noosa, Byron Bay, the Islands close to Brisbane. For holidays i went to Tasmania to hike, which was amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is very much western and like Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to pubnights and join facebook-groups and whatsapp groups for other international/exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness and kindness. Especially, my Australian professors made a great effort in asking me about my stay.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on the weekend trips with clubs at QUT or UQ, they are a great way to make friends. 
Find accomodation before going to Brisbane as there is a huge housing crisis at the moment. 
Try to have a large saving or take a SU-loan, because it will be expensive (but worth it)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of Danes, that were also on exchange and getting to travel Australia together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The planning and organising of everything was hard at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
